Hope you’re doing well. We’re starting prep for our renewal conversation and I wanted to surface a few constraints from procurement and finance so we can get aligned before a formal proposal:

- We expect a mid-contract usage increase in Nov/Dec (~30% peak) tied to a pilot with one of our product lines.

- Finance asks whether we can do a phased uplift (partial commitment now, additional committed buckets in Q1) vs. an instantaneous large uplift — they’re worried about cash timing.

Can you outline options (pro-rata top-up, voucher-style credits, annualize/don’t annualize) and any discount ranges you’d expect for a committed uplift that’s co-termed? I’ll need a short deck they can take to CFO and legal.

Emma —

Thanks for the context and the usage file. High level, we can support both patterns you described; below are three tailored options that map to common procurement preferences. I’ve kept numbers illustrative — Ben (cc) will validate margins and finalize the banding.

Option A — Immediate Uplift (single amendment)
- Add 30% committed capacity starting on amendment effective date, annualize pricing to new run-rate if co-term requested.
- Typical uplift discount: 5–10% off list for 12–24 month co-term depending on volume.
- Upside: simpler billing, single DocuSign.
- Downside: Finance may object to larger upfront spend.

Option B — Phased Uplift + Bridge Credits (preferred for cash smoothing)
- Commit to a two-stage increase: 15% effective on amendment, additional 15% auto-activates on Jan 1 (co-term alignment).
- We provide a bridge credit bucket to cover overages between amendment and Jan 1 (applied as credit against next invoice).
- Discount: 6–8% on committed uplift if co-term to Jan 1.
- Upside: lowers near-term cash impact; predictable co-term.

Option C — Voucher / True-up Model
- No immediate committed uplift; purchase an uplift voucher (prepaid credit) that converts to committed capacity if redeemed.
- Voucher discount depends on prepayment size (typically 3–7%).
- Upside: minimal contract changes.

Next steps: If you like Option B, we’ll run a simple margin check and produce a formal amendment draft + short 1-pager for CFO. Can we set a 30-min sync this week?

— Lauren Bishop

Lauren — quick pricing ops notes and a recommended structure: 

Thanks for drafting options. I ran a quick model against their Q2 usage (attached) and here’s what I’d push for from a pricing viewpoint: 

- Favor Option B as written but add a small safeguard ("fallback bucket"): if actual peak usage in Nov/Dec exceeds the committed 30% by more than 20%, we bill overage at a pre-agreed overage rate (list * 0.6) but cap the monthly overage charge to the size of the bridge credit so finance isn’t surprised. This keeps application availability while limiting spend shock.
- Proposed discount tiers for committed incremental capacity (gross uplift):
  - 0–20% uplift: 4% discount
  - 21–50% uplift: 8% discount
  - 51%+: 12% discount (requires finance approval)
- For co-term to Jan 1: we annualize the committed uplift across remaining months and apply the discount pro-rata. This is commonly acceptable to procurement.

I also prepared a sample amendment template and a DocuSign link to a mock amendment to speed legal review (internal stub).

Following up with a concise proposal based on your ask + internal pricing review. I’ve attached a short amendment and a one-page summary for CFO. The recommended path is Option B with a small tweak for noise protection:

Recommended: Option B - Phased Uplift + Bridge Credit + Fallback Cap
- Stage 1 (effective on amendment signature): +15% committed capacity, billed at co-term rate pro-rated to Jan 1.
- Stage 2 (auto-activate on Jan 1): additional +15% committed capacity to reach the 30% uplift.
- Bridge credit: $25,000 credit applied to cover Nov/Dec overage; any remaining credit flows to the Jan invoice.
- Fallback cap: if overage > 20% beyond committed uplift, overage billed at list * 0.6 but capped monthly to the size of the bridge credit.
- Discount: 7% on the uplift band (applied pro-rata when co-term confirmed).
